title: OpenHW CV32E40X
_note: The CORE-V CV32E40X: the 4-stage RV32 core with the B and M extensions, the
optional A extension, CLIC interrupts, PMA / MPU, watchpoint triggers and the
eXtension interface (CORE-V XIF).  Its own cv32e40x_manifest.flist is the
closure: rtl/include/cv32e40x_pkg.sv, every rtl/*.sv, and bhv's simulation
clock gate (the only bhv file the core instantiates).
Not rows: the RVFI tracer and its OBI shims, cv32e40x_core_log and
cv32e40x_dbg_helper (simulation-only), the sva/ assertion modules bound into
the core, and the wrapper that binds them.
SIX of the 42 rows could not be read AT ALL until Surelog acb31e60 (#4229):
cv32e40x_pma declares
`parameter pma_cfg_t PMA_CFG[PMA_NUM_REGIONS-1:0] = '{default: PMA_R_DEFAULT}`
-- an unpacked-array parameter whose element is a packed struct, defaulted
with a struct-valued expression -- and Surelog SEGFAULTED on it, so pma, mpu,
write_buffer, if_stage, load_store_unit and cv32e40x_core itself produced no
UHDM.  Probing this family is what found that defect.
First local sweep 2026-10-28: 42 rows, 35 comparable, **30 proven**, 42 / 42
with 0 undriven, 32 co-sim PASS, and **0 `read_uhdm`-only co-sim**
**divergences**.  What is left:
* SEVEN rows have no reference because `read_slang` cannot read them, and
VERILATOR SPLITS THEM IN TWO -- which is the only thing that decides
whose limitation each one is (docs/slang_unsupported.md counts a row only
when Verilator AND read_uhdm accept it):
- FOUR are genuine read_slang limits: if_stage, load_store_unit and
both obi_interface modules fail with `'obi_inst_req_t' cannot be used
in an expression`, and Verilator lints all four CLEAN.  These are the
slang_unsupported.md rows.
- THREE are NOT: align_check (`no member named 'align_status' in
'CORE_RESP_TYPE'`), controller and controller_fsm (`no member named
'we' in 'REQ_TYPE'`).  Verilator rejects all three with the SAME
complaint (`Member 'align_status' not found in structure`, `Member
'we' not found in structure`), so two independent tools agree the
member does not exist at the module's DEFAULT type parameters.
read_uhdm reads them only because it is more permissive, which is not
a result in our favour -- it is the `parameter type X = logic` class
again, and binding those types (as cheshire.json does) is what would
make these rows real.
* THREE formal-only `differs` leads: cs_registers (co-sim diverges on BOTH
readers, 301 vs 161 cycles -- a shared artefact, not ours), core (no
co-sim: its top has escaped interface ports from the CORE-V XIF), and
sequencer (co-sim PASS over 300 active cycles).  sequencer and core each
report `0 undriven (4 never assigned in the source)`, which is exactly
the shape that folds a miter trigger to a constant -- dump the optimised
miter before calling either a reader defect.
* TWO SAT-budget rows: ex_stage (whose co-sim divergence is SHARED, 273
cycles on both readers) and mult.
cv32e40s / cv32e41p / core-v-mcu are separate checkouts of the same shape and
are still to do.
